<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">cicada</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">LiberPrimus</span>
<span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">cicada</span>.<span class="pl-s1">gematria</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">Latin</span>, <span class="pl-v">Runes</span>

<span class="pl-c"># load the lp from file</span>
<span class="pl-s1">lp</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">LiberPrimus</span>()

<span class="pl-s1">shift</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">0</span>
<span class="pl-c"># for pages 0 - 3 of the lp</span>
<span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-s1">lp</span>.<span class="pl-c1">pages</span>[<span class="pl-c1">0</span>:<span class="pl-c1">3</span>]:
    <span class="pl-c"># page is a Runes() object so we can do some cool things:</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># atbash substitution</span>
    <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">atbash</span>()
    <span class="pl-c"># caesar shift</span>
    <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">shift</span>(<span class="pl-s1">shift</span>)
    <span class="pl-c"># use .text to get the contents of a Gematria() object such as Runes()</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># Note: it will also convert to str with str(Runes()) or equiv</span>
    <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Runes: %s"</span> <span class="pl-c1">%</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">text</span>)
    <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Plaintext: %s"</span> <span class="pl-c1">%</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">to_latin</span>())
    <span class="pl-c"># example of automated shifting</span>
    <span class="pl-s1">shift</span> <span class="pl-c1">+=</span> <span class="pl-c1">1</span>

<span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-en">Runes</span>(<span class="pl-s">"ᚠᚢᚦᚩᚱᚳᚷᚹᚻᚾᛁᛄᛇᛈᛉᛋᛏᛒᛖᛗᛚᛝᛟᛞᚪᚫᚣᛡᛠ"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">to_latin</span>())
<span class="pl-c"># FUTHORKGWHNIJEOPXZTBEMLINGOEDAAEYIAEA</span>
<span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-en">Latin</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Hello World!"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">to_runes</span>())
<span class="pl-c"># ᚻᛖᛚᛚᚩ ᚹᚩᚱᛚᛞ!</span>
<span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-en">Latin</span>(<span class="pl-s">"How would cicada type question everything?"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">to_runes</span>().<span class="pl-c1">to_latin</span>())
<span class="pl-c"># HOW WOULD CICADA TYPE CWESTION EUERYTHING?</span></pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

from cicada.gematria import Latin, Runes

# load the lp from file
lp = LiberPrimus()

shift = 0
# for pages 0 - 3 of the lp
for page in lp.pages[0:3]:
    # page is a Runes() object so we can do some cool things:
    # atbash substitution
    page.atbash()
    # caesar shift
    page.shift(shift)
    # use .text to get the contents of a Gematria() object such as Runes()
    # Note: it will also convert to str with str(Runes()) or equiv
    print("Runes: %s" % page.text)
    print("Plaintext: %s" % page.to_latin())
    # example of automated shifting
    shift += 1

print(Runes("ᚠᚢᚦᚩᚱᚳᚷᚹᚻᚾᛁᛄᛇᛈᛉᛋᛏᛒᛖᛗᛚᛝᛟᛞᚪᚫᚣᛡᛠ").to_latin())
# FUTHORKGWHNIJEOPXZTBEMLINGOEDAAEYIAEA
print(Latin("Hello World!").to_runes())
# ᚻᛖᛚᛚᚩ ᚹᚩᚱᛚᛞ!
print(Latin("How would cicada type question everything?").to_runes().to_latin())
